notes: HVS 22 is a named member of the Brown et al. (2018) sample reanalysed by Kreuzer et al. (2020); the paper uses its high total velocity and tangential components in its observational comparison (T:p9-b9). S5-HVS1 is explicitly discussed as the sole named >700 km s−1 exception and prior Galactic-Centre ejection, so I treat it as a follow-up comparison (T:p2-b2). HVS-1 is named only in the historical discovery summary (T:p1-b9) and is not individually analysed, so I did not count it as a follow-up. Other Brown et al./Kreuzer/Marchetti samples are not individually named in the supplied material and cannot be recorded as separate stars.

S5-HVS1: The paper reports S5-HVS1's velocity as 1700 km/s in T:p2-b2 but does not explicitly state whether this is a radial or total velocity; it is recorded here as radial velocity, the standard quantity for HVS surveys. No other quantities (position, distance, parallax, proper motion, etc.) are reported for S5-HVS1.

HVS 22: HVS 22 is mentioned only in Sect. 3.5. The reported 1530^{+690}_{-560} km/s is a total velocity with substantial tangential components, not a line-of-sight radial velocity. The text does not explicitly name the reference frame; it is treated here as a total three-dimensional speed rather than a radial velocity.
